audit.whatIsWrong: Knuckle Down (Q) deals additional damage based on the TARGET'S maximum health. Zac's prescribed core item in the full layer is Heartsteel, whose entire function is stacking maximum health, and neither layer notes the conflict.
audit.why: It means Zac's core item is partly building Sett's damage for him. Every Heartsteel stack raises the ceiling on Knuckle Down's bonus, which lands on the next two basic attacks on a 9s cooldown at rank 1 — the most frequently repeated damage in the matchup. That does not make Heartsteel wrong, but it changes what goes beside it: armour is worth more here than in a generic tank build, because armour cuts the punch while more health inflates it.
audit.corrected: Knuckle Down scales off your maximum health. Buy armour alongside Heartsteel rather than stacking raw HP first — health is the one stat that makes his most-repeated ability hit harder.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sett.json (Knuckle Down: "deal additional damage based off of the target's max health", cooldown 9/8/7/6/5)

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers treat Facebreaker (E) as a stun unconditionally — content wants.you[2] 'before the stun combo', spikes[1].text 'his Facebreaker (E) pull-stun into R combo', whys[4] 'Facebreaker (E) into The Show Stopper (R)', full dontsFull[2].t 'Get E-stunned'. Riot's text: it pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him, and 'If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.'
audit.why: The stun is conditional on Sett catching bodies on both sides of himself, and that condition is positional — it depends on where the minion wave sits relative to him, not on his cooldown. A Zac who understands this can deny the stun by not letting Sett stand between him and the wave, which is a real, repeatable piece of lane positioning. Described as an unconditional stun, it is just another thing to fear.
audit.corrected: Facebreaker (E, 16s at rank 1, 490 range) stuns only when it grabs enemies on both sides of Sett. Caught alone on one side, you are slowed instead. Watch where the wave sits relative to him.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sett.json (Facebreaker: 'pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him... If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned')

audit.whatIsWrong: Haymaker (W) deals true damage in the CENTRE of the punch and physical damage on the SIDES. Both layers describe it only as 'true damage' — full dontsFull[1].t reads 'Eat his W true damage', content whys[1] 'Haymaker (W) true damage punishes your poke attempts'.
audit.why: It is the one piece of counterplay to the biggest single hit in the matchup, and it costs nothing to use. Sett's Haymaker is on 18s at rank 1 and its damage is capped by stored Grit, so the player cannot avoid eating it forever — but he can choose where he stands when it lands, and off-centre converts true damage into physical damage his armour actually reduces.
audit.corrected: Haymaker: true damage in the centre, physical on the sides. Step off the centre line before it lands and your resistances start applying.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sett.json (Haymaker: 'dealing true damage in the center and physical damage on the sides')

audit.whatIsWrong: Flagged in the packet: Zac wins 52.91% over 223 games but the content chart gives Sett 5 of 7 stages to Zac's 2.
audit.why: A 52.91% matchup over a large sample is close to even and should not read as the enemy owning five of seven stages. I made the minimum honest change — level 2 to Skill and levels 4-5 to Zac — reaching Sett 3 / Zac 3 / Skill 1. I deliberately left level 3 with Sett even though the full layer calls it Zac, because Sett at 3 has his full basic kit and a real level-3 all-in, and flipping it to make the two layers agree would be inventing a swing.
audit.corrected: win[1] Sett -> Skill, win[3] Sett -> Zac. Chart becomes Sett, Skill, Sett, Zac, Sett, Zac, Zac.
sources: packet zac.json (winRate 52.91, games 223, defect 'level chart contradicts data')

audit.whatIsWrong: full breakdown.cooldowns says 'Sett Haymaker: matchup-defining — Shield + true damage. Knock it' with no numbers, and the content layer gives no cooldown for any Sett ability.
audit.why: The numbers reframe the lane. Haymaker is 18s at rank 1 and Facebreaker 16s, while Zac's Unstable Matter is a flat 5s — so Zac has roughly three casts of his %max-health burn per cycle of Sett's answer. 'Trade around Haymaker' is correct advice, but without the numbers the player has no idea how much room the window actually gives him.
audit.corrected: Haymaker 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s, damage capped by stored Grit. Facebreaker 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s, 490 range. Knuckle Down 9/8/7/6/5s. The Show Stopper 120/100/80s, 400 range.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sett.json (cooldowns and ranges from Riot Data Dragon)

notes: Three real finds, all from Riot's own ability text. (1) Knuckle Down deals bonus damage based on the TARGET's max health, and the full layer prescribes Heartsteel as core — Zac's own item inflates Sett's most-repeated ability. Corrected to armour alongside Heartsteel rather than raw HP first. (2) Haymaker is true damage only in the CENTRE, physical on the sides; both layers called it flatly 'true damage', losing the one free mitigation available against the biggest hit in the lane. (3) Facebreaker stuns only when it catches enemies on both sides of Sett — alone on one side you are slowed — which makes the stun a positional question about where the wave sits, not an unavoidable cooldown. Both layers treated it as an unconditional stun in four places. Chart: the packet-flagged contradiction (Sett 5/7 against a 52.91% win rate) is fixed with the minimum two cells, giving Sett 3 / Zac 3 / Skill 1. I left level 3 with Sett despite full phases[2].side='Zac' — Sett genuinely owns level 3 and flipping it only to make the layers agree would be inventing a power shift, so a residual disagreement at index 2 remains and is intentional.
